environment.description: Go WebSocket service deployed on EC2 in a private subnet (no public IP, no IGW route). Traffic arrives through an internal NLB (Network Load Balancer) with a target group health check on /healthz. The NLB listener on port 443 has TLS termination. Upstream connectivity is restricted by the VPC's route table which only has routes to 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12 prefixes. The NLB itself sits in a private subnet fronted by AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service). The endpoint service has an allowlist of specific AWS account IDs (the three internal platform accounts: 111122223333, 444455556666, 777788889999) configured via the endpoint service's allowed-principals list. Additionally, the NLB security group (supported since 2023) restricts inbound to CIDR ranges 10.200.0.0/16 and 172.16.44.0/22 which correspond to the internal corporate VPN egress and the CI/CD runner subnet respectively. DNS for the service endpoint (upload-rt.internal.corp) resolves only within the private hosted zone associated with the VPC. No public DNS record exists. The combination means only traffic originating from known internal CIDR ranges within approved AWS accounts can establish a WebSocket connection to the service.

config.tls_termination: NLB with ACM cert for upload-rt.internal.corp
config.dns: Route53 private hosted zone only, no public record
